sentences.text: Smt.Deepmala vs State Of U.P. on 20 February, 2023

Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma
Bench: Subhash Chandra Sharma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 80
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 8710 of 2022
Applicant :- Smt.Deepmala

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Bharat Bhushan Paul,Saurabh Paul Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ajai Mani Tiwari Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard Shri Saurabh Paul, learned counsel for the applicant and Shri Surendra Tiwari, learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The present anticipatory bail application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.58 of 2022, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471,504,506 IPC, Police Station Rakabganj, District - Agra.

Facts in brief are that the informant was holder of power of attorney relating to the property House No. 34/153, 34/154, 34/156 regarding which execution proceedings as Case No. 779 of 2019 are pending.

On 21.10.2021 the fact came into knowledge of the informant that co-accused Manish Chandok prepared forged will in his favour to grab the aforementioned property with the help of other co-accused persons those are members of his family including present applicant who is his wife.
It is also submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that she is innocent and has not committed any offence regarding the property in dispute in the present case.
She has been roped in this case being wife of co-accused Manish Chandok with other members of her family.
There is no any previous criminal history against the applicant.

Investigation is going on and there is apprehension Smt.Deepmala vs State Of U.P. on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80789303/
1
of arrest, therefore, requested for anticipatory bail.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, she would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid and urged that in this case applicant is the wife of main accused Manish Chandok whose bail application has been rejected by this Court and also by the Supreme Court.
It is also urged that the applicant Deepmala is wife of Manish Chandok who represented herself as wife of Manish Singh in other transactions done by her and her husband.
She has filed an affidavit before the execution court representing her as wife of Manish Singh.
In this way it cannot be said that this applicant is innocent and has not participated in the present transaction with her husband.
Likewise, mother and brother of Manish Chandok are also benefitted with the acts of co-accused Manish Chandok.
In this way applicant is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record it appears that the name of this applicant has been mentioned but no any specific role has been assigned to her while preparing the forged will-deed or as becoming the beneficiary.

There is no any previous criminal history against the applicant, therefore, without making any comment on the merit of the case there appears ground for anticipatory bail in favour of the applicant till submission of police report under Section 173(2) of Cr.P.C., therefore, applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case for the limited period considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In default of any of the conditions, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicant.
